China-Russia ties entering new stage of greater achievements with resilient cooperation at milestone of strategic partnership
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:01:16 CST
13:01:16 KST

ST. PETERSBURG, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China and Russia have leveraged more dynamic and resilient cooperation to cushion the impact of external uncertainties and instability, and bilateral ties are entering a new stage marked by greater achievements and faster development, said Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Wednesday.
Li made the remarks while co-chairing the 31st regular meeting between Chinese and Russian heads of government with Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin.
This year marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination. For three decades, the regular meeting, held every year since its inception in 1996, has served as an important mechanism for implementing the consensus reached by the two heads of state and promoting bilateral cooperation and people-to-people exchanges, no matter how the international situation evolves.
China and Russia have in recent years stood side by side and moved forward together in the face of a complex and turbulent international landscape, Li said.
"This environment calls for continuous coordination and timely adjustment of plans. By advancing all-round cooperation, our two countries (Russia and China) are effectively countering the destructive forces and trends," said Andrei Vinogradov, head of the Center for Contemporary China Studies at the Institute of Oriental Studies under the Russian Academy of Sciences.
During the regular meeting on Wednesday, both sides agreed that China and Russia should advance cooperation in key areas such as economy and trade, investment, energy and resources, foster new drivers of development in frontier areas such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology and the digital economy, jointly ensure the success of the China-Russia Years of Education, and strengthen people-to-people and cultural exchanges.
These commitments build on the strong foundation of practical cooperation between the two countries, with economic and trade ties remaining a major pillar of the bilateral relationship.
Data from China's Ministry of Commerce showed that in 2025, China-Russia trade reached 227.9 billion U.S. dollars, staying above 200 billion dollars for the third consecutive year. China remained Russia's largest trading partner for the 16th consecutive year.
The structure of bilateral trade has also continued to improve, with electromechanical and high-tech products accounting for a growing share. Chinese automobiles, home appliances and machinery have maintained strong exports to Russia, while Russia has remained a stable supplier of energy, minerals and agricultural products to China.
"It is noteworthy that the two countries are working not merely to identify new converging interests, but also to explore new development avenues by leveraging the combined potential of their two economies," Vinogradov said.
Bilateral trade maintained relatively rapid growth in 2026. Statistics from China Customs showed that in the first seven months of the year, China-Russia trade reached 159.2 billion dollars, up 26.3 percent year on year.
"Russian and Chinese economies are complementary. This allows each side to pursue its own development path and advance its national interests," said Vladimir Lvovich Nezhdanov, an expert at the Institute of Contemporary International Problems, Diplomatic Academy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation.
"Russia needs a stable and dynamically growing China, just as China needs a stable and dynamically growing Russia. This is a mutual interest," he added.
On the global dimension, a joint communique issued after the 31st regular meeting said that China and Russia firmly uphold the United Nations-centered international system and the international order based on international law. The two countries also support consolidating fair international relations on the basis of mutually beneficial cooperation among sovereign states and oppose dividing the world into rival regions or blocs, it said.
"China proceeds in a steady manner, recognizing that no initiative or policy measure can be implemented without mutual trust," said Nezhdanov, noting a white paper titled "More Just and Equitable Global Governance: China's Principles, Proposals and Actions" released by China in June.
Cultivating mutual trust under the Global Governance Initiative is a practice that major countries, which are willing to assume responsibility for international affairs, have long followed to normalize and strengthen international dialogue, he added.
This year also marks the 25th anniversary of the signing of the Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation Between China and Russia. Over the years, the two countries have always adhered to the treaty's established principle of non-alliance, non-confrontation and not targeting any third party, and stayed committed to equality, mutual respect, good faith and win-win cooperation, making important contributions to safeguarding international fairness and justice and promoting a new type of international relations, and serving as a vital constant amid century-defining changes sweeping across the world, said Xi in May during Putin's state visit to China.
The two sides should deepen multilateral coordination, further increase coordination and collaboration on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, BRICS and APEC, unswervingly uphold the postwar international order and the authority of international law, unite the Global South, and steer the reform of the global governance system in the right direction, Xi said then.
"Russia-China relations are a truly high-quality model of relations between major countries, delivering benefits and shared interests at every level, from grassroots communities to national governments and the global stage alike," Nezhdanov said. ■

13:00:49 KST

WELLINGTON, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- New Zealand's annual inflation eased to 3.7 percent in the September 2026 quarter from 4.1 percent in the previous quarter, still remaining above the central bank's target band of 1 to 3 percent, official data showed on Thursday.
Petrol was the largest contributor to annual inflation, with prices rising 19.1 percent from a year earlier. If petrol prices had remained unchanged, annual inflation would have been 3.2 percent in the period, according to a statement from Stats NZ, the country's statistics agency.
The cost of constructing new housing rose 3.2 percent over the year, with higher material, subcontractor, labor and fuel costs contributing to the increase, Stats NZ prices and deflators spokesperson Nicola Growden said in the statement.
Other major contributors to annual inflation included electricity, up 9.3 percent, international airfares, up 12.5 percent, and local authority rates and payments, up 6.2 percent, statistics showed.
More than 85 percent of items in the consumer price index (CPI) basket increased in price over the year, while about 13 percent fell in price, the lowest proportion since the December 2023 quarter, according to Stats NZ.
Quarterly, the CPI rose 0.7 percent in the September quarter from the previous quarter, with international airfares the largest upward contributor, up 14.3 percent, mainly due to higher fares to Europe and Asia, the agency said.
Petrol prices fell 6.5 percent over the quarter, after rising 20.1 percent in the June 2026 quarter, it said.
Finance Minister Nicola Willis told reporters that Thursday's inflation figures were encouraging, but overseas events and the international oil shock continued to pose pressures. ■

“Government messaging on defence and security will continue to build ahead of ALBISTON SHADOW, a major UK Home Defence exercise, and NATO’s Crisis Management Exercise in spring 2027.”
Briefing company bosses directly on the threat picture marks a change in how the state handles this material, since the intelligence assessments behind it have traditionally stayed inside government and inside cleared parts of industry. Splitting the work between the Security Minister for critical national infrastructure and the Minister for the Armed Forces for industry gives each a defined audience.
University leaders and political parties were given equivalent briefings earlier this year on foreign interference, covering Chinese and Russian activity aimed at research, funding and candidate selection. Extending the same treatment to energy, water, telecommunications and transport operators brings it to the sectors that would be targeted first in a campaign of sabotage.
Exercise ALBISTON SHADOW is the largest home defence exercise Britain has run in decades, and has been described as a test of whether the public would know what to do and where to go if the country came under attack. Pairing it with NATO’s Crisis Management Exercise puts the national and alliance rehearsals in the same window in spring 2027.

Australian hospitalizations following e-scooter falls on rise: report

Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:00:44 CST
13:00:44 KST

CANBERRA, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- The number of Australians hospitalized with injuries sustained in incidents involving e-scooters has more than tripled since 2019, according to a government report.
The report released on Thursday by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW) showed that there were 4,089 hospitalizations for falls involving powered scooters in 2024-25, up 216.7 percent from 1,291 in 2019-20.
It said that the population-wide hospitalization rate for falls involving powered scooters increased from 5.1 per 100,000 people to 14.9 per 100,000 people in the same period, while the hospitalization rate for falls involving non-powered scooters fell from 6.8 to 4.9 per 100,000 people.
According to the report, males accounted for 69 percent of hospitalizations for falls involving powered scooters. The increase in hospitalizations was largest among people aged 12-15, with the rate growing from 3.1 hospitalizations per 100,000 people in 2019-20 to 33.4 per 100,000 in 2024-25.
Among boys aged 12-15, the hospitalization rate was 54 per 100,000 compared to 12 per 100,000 for girls.
"While the data cannot tell us exactly how much of this change is due to increased use, it is consistent with the growing popularity of e-scooters in Australia over recent years," AIHW spokesperson Jacqueline Rek said in a media release.
The proportion of hospitalizations following e-scooter falls that involved fractured bones increased from 46 percent in 2015-16 to 58 percent in 2024-25.
The report noted that new hospital codes that were introduced in July will allow future data to distinguish between e-scooters, e-bikes and other mobility devices more clearly. ■

US and Israel create plans for 'short but intensive' strikes on Iran after midterms - report
The New York Times reported that American and Israeli military planners have reportedly developed options for an operation against Iran lasting roughly three days
The United States and Israel are preparing for a possible new attack on Iran after the American midterm elections, even as questions persist over whether another military campaign would secure concessions from Tehran, The New York Times reported.
The proposed campaign would concentrate strikes into roughly three days, concentrating operation on nuclear facilities, missile and drone capabilities, and parts of Iran’s energy infrastructure.
US officials and others familiar with the discussions said the United States is also assembling additional forces. Its planned deployment, including three aircraft carriers, Marines, combat aircraft and Special Operations personnel, is expected to be fully positioned by early November.
President Donald Trump has not approved an attack. The Times reported that he has repeatedly held back proposed operations, including one earlier this month that both militaries had prepared to launch.
At the center of the deliberations is a disputed calculation: whether a short burst of military force could achieve diplomatic results that months of fighting and economic pressure have failed to deliver.
Iranian officials have warned that retaliation could extend to data centers, undersea internet cables and regional oil facilities. Mahdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran’s negotiating team, called expectations of a 72-hour campaign a “fantasy.”
“Our attacks will be more fierce, creative and different,” Mohammadi wrote on social media.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Ministry of Education conducted drug-prevention sessions in more than 50,000 classes last year to help students recognize the dangers of etomidate, CNA reported.
Education Minister Cheng Ying-yao (鄭英耀) said Thursday that etomidate had become the second most common drug encountered by students since 2024, surpassing marijuana and amphetamines.
The sedative, used for general anesthesia, can cause dependence and has been mixed with chemical additives to produce liquid for e-cigarettes, according to the Keelung City Government.
Lessons on the dangers of drugs and e-cigarettes were incorporated into health and physical education courses, and the ministry reached all targeted classes last year. Through September this year, it had conducted similar sessions in more than 48,000 classes.
Cheng said emerging drugs and e-cigarettes were constantly changing in appearance, with some featuring cartoon characters or resembling USB drives and bubble tea. The ministry has stepped up efforts during school visits to teach students how to recognize these products and understand their risks.
The ministry is also considering saliva tests to help schools identify potential drug use early and has coordinated with the National Police Agency on joint procurement. The tests could be introduced after amendments to the Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act are passed.
According to the Keelung City Government, inhaling etomidate can cause hand tremors and full-body shaking. Severe cases may result in permanent neurological damage or respiratory arrest.

Russia bombs Kyiv and Ukraine fires drones towards Moscow, despite talk of renewing negotiations
KYIV, Oct 22 - Russia pounded Kyiv with ballistic missiles and Ukraine sent hundreds of drones towards Moscow overnight as the warring sides kept up a barrage of attacks despite the latest US push to end the conflict.
Russia said on Wednesday it was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month, after President Vladimir Putin hosted US envoy Steve Witkoff for talks in St Petersburg.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he hoped negotiations, which would be the first since February, would take place early in November.
Ukraine said Russia fired at least 21 ballistic missiles in three waves, and Zelenskiy said three of them carried cluster munitions — "bomblets" that disperse over a wide area and are banned by many countries because of the danger they pose to civilians. Russia's defence ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Russia said Ukraine launched 630 drones towards Moscow during the night.
The two sides held an exchange of war dead, with Moscow handing over 252 bodies and Ukraine handing over 25, according to the Belta state news agency in neighbouring Belarus. Such exchanges have accompanied moves towards talks in the past.
But while Witkoff spoke of "some degree of momentum" after meeting Zelenskiy and European and NATO officials in Oslo earlier in the week, the Kremlin expressed doubts.
"The Americans sensed some new nuances (in Oslo) and told us about this. But these nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said.
A senior Russian official, briefed on the results of the Putin-Witkoff talks, said they were relatively short and not substantive. The American brought a set of proposals drafted in Oslo and handed them to Putin for review, the person said.
Another source close to the Kremlin said the US proposals included a scenario where Ukraine would cede all of its Donbas region to Russia in return for receiving a guarantee of its future security from NATO.
Russia says it launched the war, the deadliest in Europe since World War Two, in part to prevent Ukraine from joining NATO. It has repeatedly said it would not end fighting unless Ukraine cedes more land, limits the size of its forces and is permanently barred from forming alliances.
Ukraine, which says the invasion was an unprovoked war of conquest, has long dismissed Russia's conditions as a demand for capitulation that would leave it defenceless against future Russian attacks.
US PRAISE FOR 'HUMANITARIAN' PUTIN GOES DOWN BADLY WITH KYIV
Zelenskiy's meeting with Witkoff was aimed in part at smoothing over a deterioration in relations with Washington this month, after President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and lifted sanctions on Moscow.
Kyiv says Washington failed to provide early-warning data on Russian missile launches, throttled the SpaceX satellite system used to guide Ukrainian drones, and withheld missile defence systems bought on its behalf by Europeans. Washington denies any shift in policy to intentionally hamper Ukraine's forces.
Trump has repeatedly rebuked Ukraine for attacking Russian oil refineries while saying little about far deadlier Russian attacks on Ukraine. He called for Zelenskiy to be replaced and said Russia's actions in Ukraine have been "fine".
Zelenskiy, who long avoided any criticism of the Trump administration, has increasingly pushed back against what he describes as a shift towards sympathy with Moscow.
On Thursday Zelenskiy snapped back at Witkoff for saluting Putin as a "humanitarian" during his visit to Russia, when the US envoy thanked Putin for releasing a 74-year-old American captured by Russian forces in Ukraine.
"Three waves of ballistic missiles have been launched at Kyiv by Russian 'humanitarians' since yesterday evening," Zelenskiy posted on X. "They used 21 missiles. Unfortunately, numerous sites across the city have been hit and damaged."
He said 2 people were killed and 34 injured, including 5 children, in attacks on a dozen Ukrainian regions.
Russia said it carried out a "massive strike" overnight on port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, as well as on vessels used by the Ukrainian military.
In Russia, two people were wounded near Moscow by drones launched towards the capital during the night, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram. Most of the drones were downed at long range, he added.
In the Russian border region of Belgorod, one man was killed and another wounded by Ukrainian drones, local officials said.
With the frontlines of the war largely static, both sides have escalated long-range air strikes this year. Russia has particularly targeted the Ukrainian power grid, while Ukraine has aimed at Russian oil refineries. Both have struck data centres, commercial warehouses and Black Sea shipping.
The war has ground on for more than 4-1/2 years, defying Trump's pledge during his 2024 election campaign that he could end it in a day. No breakthrough emerged from three short meetings in Istanbul last year and three rounds of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi and Geneva at the start of this year. REUTERS

'Tricolor row': What happened at Priyanka Gandhi’s son Raihan’s exhibition at Bikaner House - controversy explained
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
03:07:00 UTC
12:07:00 KST

Artist and Photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, with one of his photographs at Bikaner House, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)
NEW DELHI: A controversy erupted at Delhi’s Bikaner House after artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, alleged that the venue’s management asked him to remove around 74 photographs documenting recent youth protests ahead of his solo exhibition, “No Idea Is Final”.Raihan also alleged that he was asked to remove two photographs of the Indian flag, saying he had refused to take them down.
The exhibition opened as scheduled on Wednesday, with around 40 photographs remaining on display while more than 70 were removed, according to a PTI report. The show, featuring wildlife photography, abstract works and images of recent youth movements, is scheduled to continue until Sunday.In a post on Instagram, Raihan wrote, "Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show "No Idea Is Final", which opens this evening at 7 pm. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi. Apparently, the content is "objectionable". They also directed me to remove two photos of the Tiranga. I have refused. I will not take down a picture of the Indian flag."
Why were the photographs removed
Raihan told PTI that the management had raised objections to the “political nature” of the protest photographs. He said he was informed at 3.30 pm on Wednesday that the images had to be removed by 5 pm or the exhibition would be cancelled.
According to Raihan, the management said that, given the prevailing political climate in India, it was not the right time to display the images. He maintained that the photographs did not convey a political message and merely documented protests over the preceding six months."I felt it is my duty as an Indian artist, not just because I am doing a show right now, but it is my duty as an Indian artist to document what is going on... They are censoring the work of artists, I don't know what they are scared of. They even went to the extent of removing the picture of the Indian flag," he told PTI.Raihan also said he had shared the exhibition proposal and layout with the management well in advance and objected to the removal of nearly half the artworks less than 24 hours before the opening.A Bikaner House official told PTI that the administration was not authorised to comment on the matter.
Priyanka Gandhi, Congress leaders react
Priyanka Gandhi Vadra criticised the alleged removal of the photographs, describing it as an attempt to silence young voices."I think it's ridiculous. What do you think? He is a young boy but I suppose you know, they are muzzling the voice of the youth across the nation. So it's only expected that they'll do it to anyone," she told PTI."His photographs of the protests, not a single commentary, not a single thing that was either derogatory towards anyone, just a visual documentation of the protest. So, I mean, clearly this is the way they think. It's not a democracy anymore. Today it's him, tomorrow it'll be another artist," she added.Senior Congress leader Pawan Khera also criticised the alleged censorship, questioning why photographs documenting protests had been considered objectionable."When even the Tricolour isn’t safe from the censor’s scissors, perhaps the problem isn’t the art. It’s the regime. Just hours before @raihanrvadra was to open his art show ‘No Idea Is Final ’, 74 artworks - nearly half the exhibition - were taken down for being 'political ' by the Bikaner House. The photographs merely documented protests, and not one was derogatory or inflammatory. So what exactly was the offence?" he said.
Khera further alleged that a photograph of the Tricolour was among the works Raihan had to fight to retain. Congress MP Karti Chidambaram also condemned the alleged censorship, calling the administration's behaviour "obtuse" and "churlish."The Indian Youth Congress Legal Cell also reacted to the controversy, posting on X: "IYC Legal Cell's tweet: YOU CAN CENSOR THE FRAME. NOT THE TRUTH. Saheb dara hua hai (sir is scared)."Raihan said the exhibition would continue with the works still on display and indicated that he could seek another venue if necessary to show the full collection of protest photographs.

TOKYO, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- Chinese athletes racked up victories across multiple events on Wednesday, the third competition day of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.
On the athletics field, 33-year-old Zhou Feifei settled the men's javelin throw F55 contest with his opening attempt, earning the Chinese delegation its 100th gold medal of the Games. His throw of 37.63m set a world record, leaving the rest of the competition as a battle for second place.
In a similar feat, Liang Hongxia won the women's discus throw F11 with one decisive effort, breaking the world record with 42.19m.
In the women's 100m T35, Zhou Xia took gold in an Asian Para Games record of 13.57 seconds, adding to the title she had already claimed in the 200m T35.
"I was so tired after the race that I didn't even look at the big screen. All I wanted was to run a lap of the stadium with the national flag around my shoulders," she said. "Of these two gold medals, the first one is for me, and this second one I'd really like to dedicate to my parents."
In the women's 100m T11, visually impaired athletes raced with the help of sighted guide-runners, with each pair connected by a tether about 10cm long. At 34, veteran runner Liu Cuiqing broke the Games record to win the title.
China's swimmers maintained their strong form in the pool. Eighteen-year-old Zhu Hui won two golds in the women's 100m freestyle S8 and 50m freestyle S8. The youngest member of the Chinese delegation at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, she has since grown into a mainstay of the team.
The men's H1-5 time trial in para cycling was among the first events of the day to finish. Heavy rain fell suddenly during the morning warm-up, but Liu Qiangli braved the conditions to familiarize himself with the course. He went on to post the fastest time in the race, giving China a winning start on the road.
Chinese athletes also topped the podium in para judo, para archery and para fencing. Gu Haiyan, one of China's flagbearers at the Paris Paralympics opening ceremony, was crowned champion in the women's epee Category A final, claiming her fourth gold medal since arriving in Nagoya.
On Thursday, Li Xiaohui will compete in the wheelchair tennis women's singles final, while China will face host Japan for the gold medal in women's wheelchair basketball. ■

Longer bushfire seasons to cost Australia 4.2 bln USD annually, experts warn
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
11:05:16 CST
12:05:16 KST

CANBERRA, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- Longer bushfire seasons caused by climate change will cost Australia billions of dollars annually over the next 30 years, experts have warned.
Emergency Leaders for Climate Action (ELCA), a subsidiary of the NGO the Climate Council consisting of former fire and emergency service leaders, said in a report published on Thursday that fire seasons have grown 21 percent longer since 1979, shrinking the window for hazard reduction efforts.
It projected that more frequent major bushfires driven by climate change will cost the nation an average of 6 billion Australian dollars (4.2 billion U.S. dollars) annually over the next 30 years.
Of the projected annual cost, it said 32 percent would come from harm to health and wellbeing, 25 percent from lost trade, 20 percent from damaged businesses and public buildings, 17 percent from lost homes and 6 percent from lost work.
The report said that southeast Australia now experiences 14 more days of extreme fire weather per year than in 1998 and that the number of extreme fire-generated storms recorded from 2004 to 2024 was six-fold higher than the preceding 20 years.
It said that Australia had 10.336 fewer volunteer firefighters as of 2023-24 than four years earlier, while the number of paid positions grew by 433 in the same period.
The ELCA warned that the next two summers would pose a particularly significant risk to communities, with the impacts of climate change exacerbated by the ongoing El Nino event.
"This dangerous double act is setting the scene for record heat, flash drought, and the possibility of worsening bushfires over the coming summers," the report said.
Australia's Bureau of Meteorology said in its latest update earlier in October that El Nino was at near-record levels, with further intensification forecast. ■

UNITED NATIONS, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- United Arab Emirates (UAE) diplomat Lana Nusseibeh has joined the race for the next UN secretary-general.

Under the UN Charter, the Security Council recommends a candidate to the General Assembly for appointment as UN secretary-general.
The seven current candidates are: Ivonne A-Baki, a former Ecuadoran minister and a diplomat; Maria Fernanda Espinosa, a former UN General Assembly president and former foreign minister and defense minister of Ecuador; Rafael Grossi of Argentina, current director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency; Rebeca Grynspan, a former vice president of Costa Rica and current secretary-general of the UN Conference on Trade and Development; Olara Otunnu of Uganda, a former UN under-secretary-general; Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, Guyana's permanent representative to the United Nations; Macky Sall, a former president of Senegal.
The term for the next UN secretary-general starts on Jan. 1, 2027. ■

China Focus: Young tenants, old neighbors: China's care homes try intergenerational living
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
11:04:55 CST
12:04:55 KST

This undated file photo shows Liang Yinxia helping a senior citizen practicing calligraphy at Nanning Wuxiang Nursing Service Center in Nanning, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua)
NANNING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- At a painting class in Nanning, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region's capital in south China, lawyer Liang Yinxia lays out art supplies and guides a group of elderly residents through the lesson. On other days, she reads the news with them, takes walks or helps them use smartphones.
Liang is not employed by the care home. Since August, she has lived there, paying part of her rent with volunteer hours.
At Nanning Wuxiang Nursing Service Center, 30 hours of volunteering a month cuts the rent by 500 yuan (about 74 U.S. dollars). Forty hours earns a 750-yuan discount, while 50 hours covers the entire 1,000-yuan rent.
Liang spent four years working in hospital nursing before becoming a lawyer in 2024. The center was near her workplace, and the rent reduction appealed to her.
Applicants must be aged 22 to 40 and meet requirements, including not owning a home in Nanning. The center gives preference to people trained in social work, healthcare, psychology or law.
Other cities have adopted their own rules, as Chinese authorities explore systems of care involving volunteers trading their time for help with accommodation.
In Jinyun County, east China's Zhejiang Province, young people can stay in unused staff rooms at participating care homes and earn rent reductions by volunteering 10 to 30 hours a month. One home has housed 95 young people since the program began in 2024, with 13 living there now.
The programs remain small in scale. Four care facilities in Nanning were selected for similar trials in 2025.
Official data shows that China's population aged 60 and above exceeded 323 million by the end of 2025, accounting for about 23 percent of the national total.
WHAT BOTH GENERATIONS GAIN
Liang had years of nursing experience, but she found that getting to know her new neighbors took time. At first, she struggled to gain their trust. Gradually, residents began telling her about their past.
"The elderly have accumulated a lifetime of experience and wisdom," she said. "You can only appreciate that by getting to know them."
An 83-year-old resident surnamed Li said she now had more people to talk to and participate in activities with. When she fell behind during a video-guided class, a young volunteer explained what to do.
In Jinyun, Wu Weifeng, a young man from neighboring Jiangsu Province, moved into a care home's staff accommodation after taking a hospital job in 2024. He had struggled to find a place to rent.
"At first, I didn't know how to start a conversation. Instead, the elderly residents came over and asked about me," Wu recalled.
The experience has made him more patient with older members of his own family, he said.
At another home in Hangzhou, the provincial capital of Zhejiang, young residents teach older people how to use artificial intelligence tools, while the older residents share memories of the city and stories from their working lives. One young tenant, Qiu Shaoqi, arrived for the free room, but later found he was reluctant to leave.
There are precedents overseas. In the Netherlands, the Humanitas retirement home in Deventer has offered university students rent-free accommodation in exchange for spending at least 30 hours a month with older residents. The arrangement drew international media attention in 2015.
The OECD's 2025 Cities for All Ages report discusses intergenerational housing as one response to loneliness and housing affordability problems, citing projects in Europe and the United States.
THE CHALLENGE OF STAYING
Liang completed 30 volunteer hours in August. In September, work commitments and health problems left her four hours short. The center agreed to let her make up the difference in October.
Social workers and care staff guide the volunteers, with their services recorded and regularly assessed.
"We need to ensure the quality of volunteer services while also considering young people's circumstances," said Huang Zibiao, the center's deputy director, adding that some young people had given up plans to live at the center because their workplaces changed, or the commute became too long.
"Moving in and becoming part of the community are two different things," said Zhang Yingxi, a researcher at the National Academy of Economic Strategy under the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS).
Some young tenants may regard cheap accommodation as a temporary solution, making it difficult to maintain lasting relationships with older residents, Zhang said.
There are practical limits, too. The volunteers are not professional caregivers, and care facilities must manage safety, privacy and other risks, said Xia Xuemin, a researcher at Zhejiang University.
In Jinyun, 24 care institutions are testing a volunteer "time bank." Participants can earn points to exchange for care services or daily necessities, or transfer them to immediate family members. More than 1,000 people have signed up.
National guidelines released by Chinese authorities earlier this year encourage localities to develop systems for recording volunteer hours in mutual elderly care programs, with credits redeemable for care services or transferable to immediate family members. Volunteer hours can be recorded, and in some places, saved as credits.
However, several elderly residents at the Nanning center said they valued regular visits and conversations more than occasional group activities. They wanted someone who would keep coming back, sit down and listen. ■
This photo taken with a mobile phone shows a volunteer helping a senior citizen to use a smartphone at a care home in Jinyun County, east China's Zhejiang Province, on Oct. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Tang Tao)

Pakistani Embassy in Tehran, ECO Cultural Institute host exhibit showcasing Pakistan’s rich history
TEHRAN- A Tehran exhibition is offering visitors a journey through Pakistan’s civilizational arc—from its ancient roots to its enduring literary traditions—while spotlighting the cultural bridges between Iran and Pakistan. Titled “Pakistan Through the Ages,” the show was inaugurated on October 20, drawing diplomats, cultural officials and researchers.
Organized by the Embassy of Pakistan in Tehran in collaboration with the ECO Cultural Institute (ECI), the exhibition brings together historical photographs, calligraphy, paintings and visual records from different periods, giving visitors a broad view of Pakistan’s cultural heritage. Its title underlines the country’s historical depth and the continuity of that heritage over time.
The opening also served as a platform for discussion of the two countries’ shared civilizational legacy, the influence of Persian language and literature on the Indian subcontinent, and the scope for expanding cultural and tourism cooperation across the region.
Pakistan’s ambassador to Iran, Imran Ahmed Siddiqui, could not attend the ceremony because he was accompanying a Pakistani delegation led by Field Marshal Asim Munir. His remarks were delivered by Ismat Hassan Sial, deputy head of mission at the Pakistani Embassy.
Some excerpts from the ambassador’s remarks follow:
“There are moments when history comes alive. It is no longer just in books or on screens. It is there in a piece of pottery, a carved stone, a sculpture, a manuscript, a line of calligraphy. Tonight, here in this exhibition, ‘Pakistan Through the Ages,’ we invite the audience to experience one such journey. A journey through time. But, more important, a journey of human connections.
“Our story begins thousands of years before the creation of Pakistan. More than nine thousand years ago, in Mehrgarh, Balochistan, people demonstrated flora and fauna, made tools and built settled communities. Over time, these early communities evolved. New settlements emerged. Trade expanded. Skills developed.
“When Pakistan emerged as an independent country in 1947, it did not begin its story from zero. It carried all these centuries with it. Mehrgarh, the Indus Valley, Gandhara and a rich tradition of Islamic culture. Pakistan was new in its political form. But ancient in the civilizations that shaped it. That, for us, is what makes this exhibition so meaningful.
“Identity is not a single moment. It is a journey. A river that gathers many streams along the way. And every stream leaves something behind. For us this exhibition is an invitation to our friends to seek Pakistan through a wider lens. Not simply as a state. But as part of a culture whose story has, in so many ways, unfolded alongside the story of this ancient land.
“And perhaps this is its special power. Culture can do what politics sometimes cannot. It helps us discover what is shared. It helps us understand our common past and use it to imagine our future.
“So tonight, we celebrate more than the centuries that have passed. We celebrate the possibility of the centuries yet to come. Let us continue this conversation. Let us continue to discover each other. And let us continue building bridges through culture, knowledge and the human connections that have linked our people for centuries.
“History tells us where we came from. But culture gives us the confidence to imagine where we can go. Let’s embark on exploration of linkages awaiting us.”
Other speakers included Ambassador Muhammad Hassan, president of the ECO Cultural Institute; Anoushirvan Mohseni Bandpei, Iran’s deputy minister of cultural heritage, tourism and handicrafts for tourism affairs; and Gholam-Ali Haddad-Adel, president of the Saadi Foundation.
Following the speeches and a video screening on Pakistan’s history, the exhibition was officially inaugurated, and guests toured the exhibition while being served delicious Pakistani snacks.
The exhibition ultimately served as more than a retrospective: it was a cultural-diplomacy platform that connected historical memory with contemporary cooperation.
By pairing archival and artistic material with discussion of shared civilizational heritage, it underscored how Iran and Pakistan can build on centuries of exchange to expand cultural, academic and tourism ties.
As visitors left with a fuller picture of Pakistan’s past, the event also left a clear message: culture remains one of the most effective bridges between the two nations and the wider region.
 
Photos By Mahnaz Abdi/Tehran Times

03:00:39 UTC

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — US-based Maritime Tactical Systems said recently that the Coast Guard Administration is buying T24 drone boats for its fleet, according to a press release.
The purchase stemmed from a memorandum of understanding signed at the 2025 Taipei Aerospace and Defense Technology Exhibition between MarTac, the National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology, and Taipei-based defense contractor Confucian. MarTac’s Florida-based partner will build some of the boats, with Confucian building the rest, as the deal requires using local workers and sharing technology to ensure China-free production.
MarTac Chief Growth Officer Seamus Flatley told Taiwan News that the Coast Guard purchased 25 T24s. He added that MarTac will deliver the vessels in batches, with the first two set to ship before the end of the year.
The co-produced model has an 8.4-meter-long hull, a burst speed of more than 50 knots (92.6 kph), and a range of up to 600 nautical miles (1,111 km), with a maximum carrying capacity of 816 kg. The coastal drone vessel can also deploy smaller T12 drone boats and withstand signal interruptions, per MarTac.
Coast Guard Administration Director-General Chang Chung-lung (張忠龍) said the T24s and unmanned aerial vehicles will help expand operations, including coordinated investigations and long-range search and rescue. He added that the T24s will also assist patrol vessels as part of the administration’s intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance network, per Liberty Times.
Flatley said the purchase was made possible through testing by NCSIST and production assistance from Confucian. Confucian CEO James Lee (李志昇) said the Coast Guard chose MarTac not just for its vessels’ capabilities, but also for the firm’s commitment to a reciprocal relationship through local co-production.
Flatley also told Taiwan News that MarTac and Confucian have selected a domestic shipbuilder. He added that MarTac will work alongside it to establish a production line to build, test, and deliver locally produced T24s.

China Coast Guard Says It Monitored Philippine Resupply Mission at Contested Shoal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
03:00:00 UTC
12:00:00 KST

The China Coast Guard (CCG) said that it monitored a Philippine delivery of “living necessities” to troops stationed at Second Thomas Shoal yesterday, a month after the Philippines accused the CCG of obstructing a similar mission.
Manila undertakes periodic missions to resupply the small unit of marines stationed aboard the BRP Sierra Madre, a grounded World War II-era warship that functions as the Philippines’ foothold at the contested shoal.
In a statement yesterday that was paraphrased by Xinhua, CCG spokesperson Jiang Lue said that it had “inquired and verified the Philippine vessel conducting the delivery, and monitored the entire process.” He added that the CCG “will continue to conduct law-enforcement and rights-protection operations” in the Spratly Islands and at Second Thomas Shoal, which Beijing refers to as Ren’ai Jiao.
China claims the majority of the South China Sea, including the entire Spratly archipelago, where the Philippines currently occupies nine features. In recent years, these have become the subject of a Chinese pressure campaign that has led to confrontations between the two sides, some involving the use of ramming tactics and high-pressure water cannons by the CCG.
Second Thomas Shoal has been a particular focus of Beijing’s efforts. Yesterday’s resupply mission, which has not been confirmed by Manila, came just under a month after the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) accused the CCG of obstructing a resupply mission to the BRP Sierra Madre. The vessel was grounded on the shoal in 1999 in order to strengthen the Philippines’ claim over it, an act that China considers illegal.
According to PCG spokesperson Jay Tarriela, the mission on September 25 was “temporarily suspended after a CCG vessel carried out dangerous maneuvers” against the Philippine resupply vessel M/V Lapu-Lapu. The maneuvers “put Filipino personnel at risk” and prevented the mission from being completed, he said. In July, a Philippine marine was injured in a melee with Chinese sailors after a CCG boat carrying eight personnel approached within close range of the BRP Sierra Madre.
These incidents broke a period of relative calm at Second Thomas Shoal, following a string of increasingly dangerous confrontations between the two sides in 2023 and 2024. After a physical clash between the two sides in July 2024 that left eight Philippine naval personnel injured, including one who lost a thumb, Beijing and Manila agreed to de-escalate the situation at Second Thomas Shoal, reaching a “provisional understanding” that allowed the Philippines to resupply the Sierra Madre without hindrance.
While the agreement appeared for a time to have calmed the situation at Second Thomas Shoal and prevented it from spiraling into a broader conflict, the two sides have disputed the details of the arrangement.
China argues that the resupply operations must be reported in advance and subjected to its inspection. In its statement yesterday, for instance, the CCG stated that the Philippines had completed its resupply missions with China’s “approval,” in line with the earlier “provisional arrangement.” The Philippines does not acknowledge any obligation to comply with such conditions or inform China of resupply missions.
The recent incidents suggest that the tacit understanding to avoid further clashes at Second Thomas Shoal has now collapsed, and the feature has once again moved to the frontline of the maritime disputes between China and the Philippines.

People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
02:37:01 UTC
11:37:01 KST

People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.

Journal Reference:

Europe cannot count on American rescue, inquiry told
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
03:30:08 BST
11:30:08 KST

Europe cannot count on the United States returning to the European Arctic as the security partner and ally that Britain and Europe previously relied on, and NATO’s Article 5 is functionally moribund in the American sense, according to evidence published by the Defence Committee.
The committee, chaired by Tan Dhesi, the Labour member for Slough, examined the implications of American policy for High North security as part of its inquiry.
Dhesi said: “Our report calls for the government to reassess the JEF’s role and consider whether it should focus more on countering threats in the High North, particularly if the UK has to plan for uncertainty over US support for NATO. The UK’s presence in the Baltics, particularly in Estonia, may need to be bolstered to offset the effects of any greater JEF focus on the High North.”
Professor David Blagden of the University of Exeter told the committee: “[w]e can talk about the formal aspects of withdrawal or not but, functionally, you would probably say Article 5 in the American sense is pretty much moribund at the moment now anyway. No one really believes that the Americans are riding to the rescue if there were some situation in the Baltic states.”
The report sets out that the American 2026 National Defense Strategy outlined four lines of effort to achieve its America First strategic approach, covering defence of the United States homeland, deterring China in the Indo-Pacific through strength, increasing burden-sharing with allies and partners, and supercharging the American defence industrial base. The committee states that none of these suggest a return to greater engagement in Europe’s defence over the medium term, including the High North, and that where the Arctic is mentioned in the strategy it is in relation to American homeland defence.
The committee was told that “[e]ven if the next US President was a dyed in the wool Atlanticist—Eisenhower 2.0 or something—the US would not have the capacity to pivot back to playing the role it did in Europe and the High North”, largely because the United States perceives the maximum likelihood of conflict in East Asia as between 2027 and 2035.
On troop numbers, the report records a reported plan to cut between 25,000 and 40,000 American troops from the roughly 80,000 currently stationed in Europe, despite congressional provisions in the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act restricting reductions below 76,000 personnel, and notes that significant future reductions in fighter jets, strategic bombers, destroyers, submarines, tanker aircraft and armed drones could also follow.
The Kiel Institute calculated that replacing American military capabilities with European weapons would cost an extra €50 billion each year over the next decade.
Professor Blagden also told the committee: “[t]he caveat, though, to all that glass-half-full stuff is that the UK, for years and years, has been generating SDSR-type documents in which we talk about how far we lean on allies. It has ultimately reached the point where the greatest of those allies has suddenly become unreliable… [w]e cannot just say, ‘We lean on an ally for this. We lean on an ally for that.’ When it comes to the High North, the UK is the major power now. The American cavalry is not about to ride over the horizon and save our fecklessness.”
Ministry of Defence witnesses drew a distinction between American capabilities and American commitments. On capabilities, the department said the United States is making it known to the rest of NATO that “[h]ere are the capabilities we [America] intend not to offer in the future. That is what we think a more European NATO looks like…” On commitments, Brigadier Jeremy Lamb, Head of Euro-Atlantic Security at the department, told the committee that “[w]hat they are talking about, is basing; it is not necessarily what they will make available to the SACEUR (Supreme Allied Commander Europe) in a crisis.”

Hackers Exploited the PHP Vulnerabilities Days Before They Were Patched
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
02:24:17 UTC
11:24:17 KST

The internet’s mad scramble on Wednesday to patch a pair of critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used web scripting language, was already too late to stop every attack, newly released details reveal.
Wednesday’s release of fixes for two critical vulnerabilities in PHP caused administrators and security staff to race to identify and patch vulnerable websites and apps, while attackers inevitably reverse engineered the fixes to learn how to exploit the flaws. Some governments and other groups even proactively took key websites down in anticipation of the release, so they wouldn't be targeted before they could apply the patches.
But in addition to detecting such active exploitation on Wednesday, research published Wednesday evening by Amazon Web Services indicates that at least one actor had started attempting to exploit the bugs—known collectively as PHP2Shell—on October 17, four days before Wednesday's public revelations.
AWS analysts spotted the October 17 exploitation on Wednesday while looking back at activity on one of their so-called honeypots, or intentionally vulnerable web servers or other digital lures that help researchers study attack methods and trends. The attempt came from an IP address that AWS says is linked to a “commercial anonymization network,” in other words a proxy network or VPN.
“While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure,” CJ Moses, AWS's chief information security officer, wrote in the research post.
Elizabeth Barron, executive director of the PHP Foundation, tells WIRED that the organization was unaware of AWS's research prior to publication and did not immediately have a comment on the findings. She added, “Although we agree that upgrading is absolutely imperative, to our knowledge, there has been no successful attempt at remote code execution.”
Proof-of-concept exploits for PHP2Shell began emerging publicly on Wednesday, with some seeming to appear hours before the public disclosure at 10 am ET. In the hours leading up to the disclosure, AWS researchers say their honeypots were hit with multiple exploitation attempts anonymized using various providers and seemingly with various attack goals, likely indicating multiple different actors. “Technical analysis is ongoing, and it’s unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems,” Moses wrote. He added that “PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild.”
Though it is unclear how the exploitation on October 17 happened or where it came from, AWS emphasizes that the findings underscore how coordinated vulnerability disclosure must evolve and speed up, given global access to AI tools that can accelerate vulnerability analysis and allow less technically proficient actors to quickly develop new exploits.
“The time from patch to working exploit is shrinking for structural reasons,” Moses wrote. “In the past, most exploitation we observed came after a public proof of concept was released. A small number of capable actors built exploits, and everyone else waited for them. That dependency is weakening. AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a patch diff or advisory into a working exploit. As a result, more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed.”
Updated 10/22/2026 at 10:10 am ET to include comment from the PHP Foundation.

House prices down in all Australian capitals in 15-year first
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
10:14:52 CST
11:14:52 KST

SYDNEY, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- House prices fell across every Australian capital city for the first time in 15 years during the third quarter of 2026, according to industry data released on Thursday.
The quarterly house price report from residential real estate marketplace Domain revealed that the combined capital city median house price fell 4.7 percent between June and September, the largest quarterly decline on record, while median unit prices declined 3.5 percent.
The report said it was the second consecutive quarter of falling prices for both property types and that annual price growth turned negative for the first time in over three years.
It noted that house prices fell in the capital cities of all eight Australian states and territories for the first time in 15 years.
In Sydney, Australia's most expensive property market, the median house price fell by 4.7 percent over the quarter to a two-year low.
Perth, capital of Western Australia, recorded a quarterly house price fall of 7.4 percent and a unit price fall of 6.5 percent, both of which were the largest declines of any capital.
Domain attributed the nationwide downturn to lower buyer confidence as a result of interest rate rises, cost-of-living pressures and the federal government's move to wind back tax concessions for property investors.
"What began as weakness concentrated in some cities has broadened considerably," Nicola Powell, Domain's Chief Residential Economist, said.
"Confidence has become one of the market's biggest headwinds. Higher interest rates and persistent cost-of-living pressures are reducing how much buyers can borrow and their willingness to transact. When buyers expect prices could fall further, there is less urgency to act and greater incentive to wait."
The Reserve Bank of Australia's Monetary Policy Board at the end of September voted unanimously to raise the cash rate target to a 15-year high of 4.60 percent.
The board will next meet to consider the key interest rate early in November. ■

NEW YORK, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- A chemical tank ruptured Tuesday night in Toledo, Ohio, leaking toxic glycidyl methacrylate gas into the air, forcing nearly 1,000 residents to evacuate and prompting a shelter-in-place order for over 50,000 people.
The 5,500-gallon tank leaked after a transfer error, Toledo Mayor Wade Kapszukiewicz said at a news conference on Wednesday, adding that authorities were waiting for the chemical to vent out of the tanker rather than trying to "actively stop the leak", which risks an explosion.
At least 35 people were treated at hospitals for minor symptoms like eye or throat burning, a sheriff's deputy was treated after feeling unwell, and schools were closed, local media reported on Wednesday.
The Toledo Fire and Rescue has reduced the evacuation zone to a half-mile radius and lifted the shelter-in-place order.
Glycidyl Methacrylate, a flammable industrial coating and plastic additive that is stored as a liquid and turns into a gas when released into the air, can cause skin, eye, and throat irritation. ■

Passive component stocks rebounded as investors bought shares that had recently suffered significant losses. Walsin Technology, Prosperity Dielectrics, Taiwan Chinsan Electronic Industrial, Viking Tech, King Core Electronics, and Max Echo Technology all rose by their daily limits.
Industry leaders Yageo and Holy Stone Enterprise each gained 2% to 3%.
High-end printed circuit board (PCB) material stocks advanced amid the ongoing Taiwan Printed Circuit Association (TPCA) Show and tight supply of ultra-low-loss materials used in high-speed AI servers. Ventec Electronics, ShineMore Technology Materials, and Iteq all rose by their daily limits, according to Sinotrade.
In contrast, glass fiber fabric stocks, another part of the PCB supply chain, retreated after broad gains in the previous session driven by the TPCA Show and expectations of higher raw material prices. Glotech Industrial fell 6.35%, Fulltech Fiber Glass declined 4.55%, and Taiwan Glass lost 0.3%.
Concord Securities investment director Liao Chi-hung (廖繼弘) said the rebound lacked broad-based strength. Buying in TSMC near the close accounted for much of the index’s gains Wednesday, according to CTEE.
Liao said the TAIEX could face resistance near 48,000 points, where heavy trading last week left many investors holding shares purchased at higher prices. He expected the index to trade between 46,000 and 48,000 points in the near term before attempting to move higher.
Liao said concerns over AI investment costs and returns, along with competition from China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies in the memory market, had weighed on technology stocks. Higher-than-expected US inflation data, elevated US Treasury yields, a weaker Taiwan dollar, and foreign investor selling had also contributed to the market correction.
With the US midterm elections scheduled for Nov. 3, Liao said historical market performance following previous midterm elections offered grounds for optimism about Taiwan stocks. He expected the TAIEX to move higher after the current consolidation, potentially testing 50,000 points in November or December.
However, Liao cautioned that market swings had widened, with more stocks pulling back quickly after reaching new highs. He advised investors to time trades carefully and avoid buying at elevated prices.

Canada's Carney visits Turkey in push to ease US trade dependence
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
02:06:27 UTC
11:06:27 KST

Canada, Turkey sign 'strategic partnership' during Carney visit meant to boost trade and investment
ANKARA, Oct 22 - Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney met with President Tayyip Erdogan in Turkey on Thursday, in the first bilateral visit by a Canadian leader, and the two NATO allies upgraded their relations to a "strategic partnership" as Ottawa seeks to expand trade partners and reduce reliance on the United States.
The new partnership would focus on trade and investment, defence and security, energy, and people-to-people ties and would aim to create jobs and boost opportunities for Canadian and Turkish companies to do more business together.
At the ceremony, Canadian and Turkish ministers signed agreements on cooperation in energy, defence and air transport.
Carney is on a global trade blitz that he hopes will help buffer Canada from a trade war with the US, where President Donald Trump has applied sweeping tariffs and questioned the neighbouring country's sovereignty.
Speaking next to Erdogan at his presidential palace in Ankara, Carney said the strategic partnership would have four pillars and include a three-year action plan.
"We’ve planted the seeds of something new: a strategic partnership that will create new opportunities for our workers and businesses, and greater security and prosperity for both our peoples. With care and commitment, it will grow for generations to come," Carney said.
NATO member Turkey is seeking new investment and collaboration for its burgeoning defence industry, new nuclear power plants and mining sector.
Praising Carney as a leader with "common-sense and acumen" on the world political stage, Erdogan said the two countries took a historic step on Thursday to deepen their cooperation.
"Today, we have alleviated the long-standing Turkey-Canada disconnect. Now, we are starting a new era between Turkey and Canada," Erdogan said, adding that the two sides expected to raise their trade volume to $5 billion first and then to $10 billion, from the current $3 billion.
Negotiators from the NATO allies would convene next month in Ankara to kick off the first round of free trade talks, Carney said, adding that Export Development Canada and Turkey's Eximbank would sign a new deal to help companies from both countries cooperate on projects in third nations.
A Turkish diplomatic source said Canadian and Turkish energy ministers would work on areas such as nuclear energy, critical minerals, and liquefied natural gas (LNG).
Carney said he would meet with prominent Turkish business leaders and investors in Istanbul on Friday.
"GEOPOLITICAL NECESSITY"
Although trade between Canada and Turkey is tiny – Turkey accounted for less than 0.3% of Canada’s total merchandise trade or C$4.34 billion ($3.09 billion) – bilateral trade has risen by nearly 50% in the past five years.
“This trip is part of the geopolitical necessity of signaling to Americans that we are not sitting around waiting for them,” said Bessma Momani, professor of political science at the University of Waterloo.
In the last year, Canada has signed more than 20 trade deals as part of Carney’s push to double non-US exports in the next decade. He flew to Beijing in January to reset fractured relations with China, striking a deal that slashed tariffs on electric vehicles and canola.
Despite criticism that China is a security risk, given Canadian authorities previously found China had interfered in at least two federal elections, Carney has described China as a “more predictable” trading partner than the US.
However, Canada still sends nearly 70% of exports to the US.
Turkey's crackdown on the opposition since 2024 and arrests targeting the LGBTQ+ community have drawn criticism. But Carney has focused less on rights than his predecessors.
“Carney will have to walk a very fine line in Turkey between opening new economic possibilities for Canada while trying to maintain Canada’s middle power role in fighting for equality,” said Anna Agathangelou, a professor of politics at York University.
Ankara says the judiciary is independent, denying that investigations or court cases are politically motivated.
At the NATO leaders' summit in July, Carney and Erdogan launched negotiations for a free-trade agreement, where Turkey also agreed to join Canada’s Defence, Security and Resilience Bank as a founding member.
Turkey has held talks with Canadian engineering firm AtkinsRealis <ATRL.TO> as well as South Korea's Korea Electric Power Corporation and China's State Power Investment Corporation about potentially building its planned second and third nuclear power plants.
In 2024, Canada removed weapons-export controls on Turkey, including on optical technology used in drones that Turkey exports to dozens of nations. Canada mainly exports lentils, aircraft and electronics to Turkey, and imports medical devices, fishing vessels, aircraft engines and jewelry. REUTERS

A rock plunged 90 kilometers into Earth and revealed something unexpected
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
01:35:57 UTC
10:35:57 KST

A rock plunged 90 kilometers into Earth and revealed something unexpected
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Göttingen
- Summary:
- Scientists discovered a rock in Papua New Guinea that plunged more than 90 kilometers beneath Earth's surface, revealing a bizarre temperature pattern that challenges established theories of Earth's interior. The unexpected shift from unusually hot to relatively cold conditions could transform our understanding of tectonic plate movements, earthquakes, and volcanoes.
- Share:
A remarkable rock discovered in Papua New Guinea has revealed an unexpected temperature pattern deep beneath Earth's surface, challenging scientists' understanding of how tectonic plates move into the planet's interior.
An international research team led by Göttingen University found that the rock traveled more than 90 kilometers (56 miles) underground about four million years ago. Along the way, it experienced unusually high temperatures at shallower depths before entering conditions associated with a relatively cooler type of subduction.
The discovery raises new questions about how heat is distributed inside Earth and how tectonic plates behave as they descend. The findings were published in Nature Geoscience.
A Strange Discovery Deep Beneath Earth's Surface
Earth's outer shell is divided into enormous tectonic plates that slowly move across the planet. When two plates converge, one can be forced beneath the other and sink into Earth's interior. This process is called "subduction."
These regions play a major role in shaping our planet. They are associated with powerful earthquakes and volcanic activity, but they also help regulate Earth's climate over millions of years by recycling materials such as carbon dioxide through the planet's interior.
The immense pressure found in subduction zones can transform rocks into a distinctive red and green material known as "eclogite." Researchers examined one of these rocks from Papua New Guinea using several advanced analytical techniques.
Inside the rock, they discovered tiny crystals of coesite, a mineral that can form only under extremely high pressure. These crystals had become trapped within another mineral as the rock formed, preserving valuable evidence of the conditions it experienced deep underground.
By studying these microscopic clues, the scientists determined that the rock had descended at least 90 kilometers beneath Earth's surface, where temperatures reached approximately 800°C (1,472°F).
Even more surprising was what they uncovered about its earlier journey.
An Unexpected Shift From Hot to Cold Subduction
The researchers reconstructed the rock's temperature history and found that at a depth of approximately 45 kilometers (28 miles), it had already reached temperatures of around 700°C (1,292°F).
That meant the rock was only about 100°C cooler at half its maximum depth, even though it still had another 45 kilometers to descend.
This was unexpected because existing models predict a different distribution of heat within subduction zones. The rock appears to have experienced unusually hot conditions at shallower depths before entering an environment with a relatively cooler temperature pattern farther down. Although its actual temperature increased with depth, the rate of warming was much smaller than scientists would normally expect.
Dr. Jan Schönig at Göttingen University's Geoscience Center explains: "Finding this change from hot to cold subduction was unexpected as this contradicts our current thermal models of subduction zones."
Scientists have previously discovered rocks containing evidence of unexpectedly high temperatures. However, this is the first time researchers have been able to reconstruct such a clear transition between different thermal conditions as a rock descended from shallower to much greater depths.
What Could Explain Earth's Hidden Heat Mystery?
The researchers have identified several possible explanations for the unusual temperature pattern.
One possibility is that tectonic plates generate substantially more heat at relatively shallow depths than scientists previously believed. As the plates move against each other, intense shearing forces could produce additional heating along their boundaries.
Another explanation is that the subduction zone had not yet existed long enough to develop the cooler temperatures predicted by conventional models.
Both processes may also have contributed to the rock's unusual thermal history.
Understanding these temperature differences is important because subduction zones influence some of Earth's most powerful geological processes. More accurate models could help scientists better evaluate the conditions associated with earthquakes and volcanic activity.
The findings could also improve our understanding of major geochemical cycles, particularly the long-term carbon cycle, which helps regulate Earth's climate by moving carbon between the surface and the planet's interior.
By revealing how conditions change as tectonic plates descend, the discovery offers scientists a new way to investigate how subduction has operated over millions to billions of years and how these processes continue shaping Earth today.
The research received funding from the German Research Foundation (DFG).
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Göttingen. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Jan Schönig, Silvio Ferrero, Kerstin Gresky, Dominik Sorger, Axel K. Schmitt, Bernd Wunder, Suzanne L. Baldwin, Adam F. Holt. Geothermal gradient change during subduction recorded by ultrahigh-pressure eclogite. Nature Geoscience, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41561-026-02110-1

China edges U.S. for first women's team world gymnastics title in 20 years
